guardrails.no_p_hacking: Each is registered ONCE with fixed parameters before running. Failures are reported and the variant dropped; no parameter sweeps.
guardrails.multiple_testing_disclosure: These are the 11th-13th variants on the same data. Accumulated searching is itself a statistical cost: the more variants tried, the more likely one looks good by luck. Treat any single winner with more suspicion than the first result, and confirm on real-option data before promoting anything.
guardrails.same_deviations: Proxied IV, constant-IV repricing, model credit -> UPPER BOUND.

trial_accounting.note: same universe/structures; these are policy refinements, but see the multiple-testing disclosure.

promotion: No promotion. SHADOW research. v5 stays live; v10 remains the leading candidate unless one of these clearly beats it.
objective: STRIKE SELECTION lever (never tested): sell further out of the money. Every variant has used ~30-delta short strikes. v12 uses ~16-delta (roughly 1 standard deviation).
philosophy: Rather than filtering WHICH days to trade, change WHERE on the curve we sell. 16-delta means smaller credit but a materially higher probability of profit and a wider buffer before the short strike is threatened -- a different risk/reward point on the same signal.
change: SHORT_PUT_DELTA -0.30 -> -0.16 and SHORT_CALL_DELTA +0.30 -> +0.16. Everything else identical to v10 (200-day put gate, call momentum gate, POP floor, $1,000 cap, 50% target).
predictions: credit per trade falls (less premium collected further OTM)
number of candidates passing the POP>=0.51 floor rises (further OTM = higher POP)
total PnL direction is genuinely uncertain: fewer/smaller wins vs fewer losses
risk: Further OTM collects less premium per unit of risk; if the loss frequency does not fall enough, return-on-risk gets worse.
